title.zh: 卷二百八十九 列傳第四十八 高瓊 范廷召 葛霸
title.en: Volume 289 Biographies 48: Gao Qiong, Fan Tingzhao, Ge Ba
title.raw: 卷二百八十九 列傳第四十八 高瓊 范廷召 葛霸 Volume 289 Biographies 48: Gao Qiong, Fan Tingzhao, Ge Ba

sentences.zh: 高瓊，家世燕人。

translations.literal: Gao Qiong—his family for generations were men of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiong came from a family of Yan men.

sentences.zh: 祖霸，父乾。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Ba; his father was Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Ba and his father Qian.

sentences.zh: 五代時，李景據江南，潛結契丹，歲遣單使往復。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period, Li Jing held the Jiangnan region, secretly allied with the Khitan, and each year sent lone envoys back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, Li Jing controlled the lands south of the Yangzi and maintained a clandestine tie with the Khitan, dispatching sole envoys to and fro each year.

sentences.zh: 霸將契丹之命，以乾從行使景。

translations.literal: Ba carried Khitan orders, taking Qian as attendant to go as envoy to Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ba bore the Khitan commission, with Qian accompanying him as envoy to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 方至江左，諜間北使與中夏構隙，以紓疆場之難，遂殺霸，居乾濠州，聲言為汴人所殺。

translations.literal: Just as they reached the lands east of the Yangzi, spies sowed discord between the northern envoy and the Central Kingdom to ease border troubles, then killed Ba, kept Qian at Haozhou, and publicly claimed he had been killed by men of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Jiangnan region, agents provoked a breach between the northern envoy and the Song court to relieve pressure on the frontier. They killed Ba, detained Qian at Haozhou, and spread word that Bian men had slain him.

sentences.zh: 乾在濠州生三子，以江左蹙弱，尋挈族歸中朝，給田亳州之蒙城，因土著焉。

translations.literal: Qian bore three sons at Haozhou; because the Jiangnan lands were pressed and weakened, he soon brought his clan back to the Central Court, was granted land at Mengcheng in Bozhou, and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: While at Haozhou Qian fathered three sons. Finding the southland increasingly precarious, he soon returned with his kin to the Song court, received farmland at Mengcheng in Bozhou, and made his home there.

sentences.zh: 瓊少勇鷙無賴，為盜，事敗，將磔於市，暑雨創潰，伺守者稍怠，即掣釘而遁。

translations.literal: In youth Qiong was fierce and reckless, became a bandit; when his affair failed and he was about to be dismembered in the marketplace, summer rain caused his wounds to split open; waiting until his guards slackened slightly, he pulled free the nails and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Qiong was violent and unruly. Caught as a robber and condemned to public dismemberment, he had the good fortune of a summer downpour that reopened his wounds. When his jailers relaxed their watch, he tore loose the nails and fled.

sentences.zh: 事王審琦，太宗尹京邑，知其材勇，召置帳下。

translations.literal: He served Wang Shenqi; when the Emperor Taizong was prefect of the capital region, knowing his talent and courage, he summoned and placed him in his personal retinue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Wang Shenqi. When Prince Taizong governed the capital district and learned of his ability and valor, he took Qiong into his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗侍宴禁中，甚醉，及退，太祖送至苑門。

translations.literal: Taizong once attended a banquet in the palace, became very drunk, and upon retiring, Taizu saw him to the garden gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after drinking heavily at a palace feast, Taizong withdrew so intoxicated that Taizu escorted him as far as the imperial garden gate.

sentences.zh: 時瓊與戴興、王超、李斌、桑讚從，瓊左手執靮，右手執鐙，太宗乃能乘馬。

translations.literal: At that time Qiong followed with Dai Xing, Wang Chao, Li Bin, and Sang Zan; Qiong with his left hand held the reins and with his right hand the stirrup, and only then could Taizong mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was among those attending—Dai Xing, Wang Chao, Li Bin, and Sang Zan—and held the bridle in his left hand and the stirrup in his right so that Taizong could mount.

sentences.zh: 太祖顧瓊等壯之，因賜以控鶴官衣帶及器帛，且勖令盡心焉。

translations.literal: Taizu looked back and admired Qiong and the others for their strength, and so bestowed upon them the robes, belts, vessels, and silks of the Crane-Control office, and moreover urged them to serve with full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu glanced back, impressed by their sturdy presence, and rewarded them with the insignia, robes, and gifts of the Crane-Control Guard, exhorting them to give their utmost in service.

sentences.zh: 會有龍騎亡命卒數十人，因知州臧丙出郊，謀劫其導從以叛。

translations.literal: There happened to be several dozen outlawed Dragon Cavalry soldiers who, learning that Prefect Zang Bing was going to the suburbs, plotted to seize his escort and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Some thirty-odd deserters from the Dragon Cavalry learned that Prefect Zang Bing was leaving the city and planned to ambush his escort and rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 瓊聞即白丙，趣還城，因自率從卒數十人，挾弓矢單騎追捕，至榆林村，及之。

translations.literal: Qiong heard and immediately reported to Bing, urging a swift return to the city; then personally leading several dozen attendant soldiers, carrying bow and arrows, he rode alone in pursuit, reaching Yulin Village and catching up with them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong at once informed Bing and urged him back to the city, then set out with some forty men, bow in hand, riding alone in pursuit until he overtook the fugitives at Yulin Village.

sentences.zh: 賊入村後舍，登牆以拒。

translations.literal: The bandits entered a rear dwelling in the village and climbed the wall to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels barricaded themselves in a cottage at the rear of the village and fought from atop its wall.

sentences.zh: 賊首青腳狼者注弩將射瓊，瓊引弓一發斃之，遂悉擒送於州。

translations.literal: The bandit chief called Green-Foot Wolf fitted his crossbow and was about to shoot Qiong; Qiong drew his bow and with one shot killed him, then captured them all and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader, known as Green-Foot Wolf, aimed a crossbow at Qiong; Qiong answered with a single arrow and brought him down, then took the entire band prisoner and delivered them to the prefectural authorities.

sentences.zh: 丙上其事。

translations.literal: Bing memorialized the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Bing reported the exploit to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會將北伐，召歸。

translations.literal: Just as a northern campaign was about to be launched, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When preparations began for a northern expedition, he was summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 授馬步軍都軍頭、領薊州刺史、樓船戰棹都指揮使，步船千艘赴雄州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief of Combined Horse and Foot Armies, concurrently Prefect of Jizhou, and Commander of Tower-Ship Battle Oars, and led a thousand infantry vessels to Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as chief of the combined horse-and-foot forces, concurrent prefect of Jizhou, and commander of tower ships, and sailed a thousand craft to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 又城易州。

translations.literal: He also fortified Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He further built up the defenses of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，為天武右廂都指揮使、領本州團練使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he became Commander of the Right Wing of the Heavenly Martial Guard and concurrently Regimental Commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made commander of the right wing of the Heavenly Martial Guard and regimental commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷左廂，改領富州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong era, he was transferred to the left wing and changed to hold the regimental commissionership of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he moved to command of the left wing and took the regimental commission at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是秋，出為單州防禦使，改貝州部署。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as Defender of Danzhou, then was changed to Deployments Commissioner of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was posted out as military defender of Danzhou, then reassigned as deployment commissioner at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 其出守也，與范廷召、王超、孔守正並命焉。

translations.literal: When they were sent out as frontier commanders, Fan Tingzhao, Wang Chao, and Kong Shouzheng were appointed together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao, Wang Chao, and Kong Shouzheng received provincial postings at the same time he did.

sentences.zh: 數月，廷召等皆復補兵職，瓊頗悒悒。

translations.literal: After several months, Tingzhao and the others were all restored to military posts, and Qiong was rather despondent.
translations.idiomatic: Within months his peers were all back in active military command, while Qiong brooded over his seeming demotion.

sentences.zh: 時王承衍鎮貝丘，公主每入禁中，頗知上於瓊厚，承衍每寬慰之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chengyan held Beiqu; the princess whenever she entered the palace knew well that the emperor held Qiong in high regard, and Chengyan often comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyan was then posted at Beiqu. The princess, on her visits to court, knew how highly the emperor esteemed Qiong, and Chengyan repeatedly reassured him.

sentences.zh: 二年，召還。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 故事，廉察以上入朝，始有茶藥之賜，至是特賜瓊焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, only surveillance commissioners and above received tea and medicine when coming to court; on this occasion Qiong was specially granted them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom only provincial surveillance commissioners and higher ranks received the imperial gifts of tea and medicine on entering court; Qiong was exceptionally granted them on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 三月，遷朔、易帥臣，制授瓊侍衛步軍都指揮使、領歸義軍節度，廷召輩始加觀察使，不得與瓊比。

translations.literal: In the third month he was transferred among the commanders of Shuozhou and Yizhou; by imperial order Qiong was made Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Soldiers and concurrently Military Governor of the Guiyi Army; Tingzhao and his ilk were only then made Surveillance Commissioners and could not compare with Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, as frontier commanders were reshuffled, Qiong was appointed commander of the palace guard infantry and military governor of the Guiyi Army—ranks that Tingzhao and the others, newly promoted only to surveillance commissioner, could not match.

sentences.zh: 出為幷州馬步軍都部署，時潘美亦在太原，舊制，節度使領軍職者居上，瓊以美舊臣，表請居其下，從之。

translations.literal: He went out as Combined Horse-and-Foot Deployment Commissioner of Bingzhou; at that time Pan Mei was also at Taiyuan; by old regulation military governors holding army posts ranked above; Qiong, treating Mei as an old minister, memorialized asking to rank below him, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as deployment commissioner of Bingzhou's horse and foot forces, he found Pan Mei already at Taiyuan. Though military governors normally outranked such posts, Qiong petitioned to serve beneath the senior Mei, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 戍兵有以廩食陳腐嘩言者，瓊知之，一日，出巡諸營，士卒方聚食，因取其飯自啖之，謂眾曰：「今邊鄙無警，爾等坐飽甘豐，宜知幸也。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers murmured about rotten grain rations; Qiong learned of it; one day inspecting the camps, soldiers were just gathering to eat; he took their rice and ate it himself, saying to the crowd: "Now the frontier is without alarm—you sit and eat full and sweet fare; you should know your good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops grumbled about spoiled rations, Qiong rode out to inspect the camps. Finding soldiers at their meal, he took a bowl and ate with them, telling the men: "The border is quiet and your bellies are full—you ought to count yourselves fortunate."

sentences.zh: 」眾言遂息。

translations.literal: The crowd's talk then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The muttering subsided at once.

sentences.zh: 改鎮州都部署。

translations.literal: He was changed to Deployment Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as deployment commissioner at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道中，就改保大軍節度，典軍如故。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era he was concurrently changed to Military Governor of the Baoda Army, commanding troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao reign he was further appointed military governor of the Baoda Army while retaining command of the troops.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加彰信軍節度，充太宗山陵部署，復為幷代都部署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Qiong was given the additional title of Military Governor of the Zhangxin Army, appointed supervisor of Emperor Taizong's mausoleum works, and again made Combined Bing-Dai Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Zhenzong's accession, Qiong received the additional post of military governor of the Zhangxin Army, oversaw construction of Taizong's tomb, and was again placed in command of the Bing and Dai deployment.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹犯塞，其母車帳至狼山大夏。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era the Khitan raided the frontier; the Khitan empress dowager's royal tent reached Langshan and Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping the Khitan breached the border, and the empress dowager's camp advanced as far as Langshan and Daxia.

sentences.zh: 上親巡河朔，遣楊允恭馳往，召瓊率所部出土門，與石保吉會鎮、定。

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured Hebei, dispatched Yang Yonggong posthaste to summon Qiong to lead his command out through Tumen Pass and join Shi Baoji at Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured Hebei in person and sent Yang Yonggong racing ahead to summon Qiong to march his troops through Tumen Pass and rendezvous with Shi Baoji at Zhenzhou and Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而傅潛以逗留得罪，即召瓊代之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fu Qian was punished for delay, and Qiong was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian was soon convicted of dallying on campaign, and Qiong was called up to take his place.

sentences.zh: 兵罷，復還本任。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended, he returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting he resumed his original command.

sentences.zh: 轉運使言其政績，詔褒之。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported his administrative achievements, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner commended his record of governance, and the throne issued a decree of praise.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，代還，以手創不任持笏，詔執梃入謁，授殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, upon returning from replacement duty, because an old hand wound prevented him from holding the court tablet, he was ordered to enter audience bearing a staff and was appointed Commander of the Palace Front Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, returning from a tour of duty, he could not grip the court tablet because of an old wound to his hand; the emperor permitted him to attend audience with a staff and appointed him commander of the palace front guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，范廷召、桑讚所將邊兵臨敵退衄，言者請罪之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the frontier troops led by Fan Tingzhao and Sang Zan had retreated before the enemy; critics called for their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan Tingzhao and Sang Zan had withdrawn their border forces in the face of the enemy, and memorialists demanded they be punished.

sentences.zh: 以問瓊，瓊對曰：「兵違將令，於法當誅。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked Qiong, Qiong replied: "Soldiers who disobey their commanders ought by law to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Asked for his view, Qiong answered: "By military law, troops who defy their generals deserve death."

sentences.zh: 然陛下去歲已釋其罪，今復行之，又方屯諸路，非時代易，臣恐眾心疑懼。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty already pardoned them last year; to punish them again now, while they are still garrisoned on many routes and this is not a time of changing commanders, I fear the men will grow doubtful and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty pardoned them only last year. To punish them again now, with armies still stationed on every frontier and no change of command imminent, would only breed fear and distrust among the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 景德中，車駕北巡。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era the imperial carriage toured north.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde the emperor marched north in person.

sentences.zh: 時前軍已與敵接戰，上欲親臨營壘，或勸南還，瓊曰：「敵師已老，陛下宜親往，以督其成。

translations.literal: At that time the vanguard was already engaged with the enemy; the emperor wished to visit the camps in person; some urged a return south; Qiong said: "The enemy army is already worn down—Your Majesty should go in person to press the victory to completion."
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard was already fighting when the emperor proposed visiting the front. Some counseled retreat to the south, but Qiong said: "The enemy is exhausted. Your Majesty should go yourself and drive the victory home."

sentences.zh: 」上悅，即日進幸澶淵。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and that same day advanced to Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor pressed on to Chanyuan that very day.

sentences.zh: 明年，以罷兵，料簡兵卒諸班直十年者出補軍校，年老者退為本班剩員。

translations.literal: The next year, because hostilities had ceased, soldiers of the various guard companies who had served ten years were selected to fill out the ranks of army officers; the aged were retired as surplus members of their original companies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with peace restored, guardsmen of ten years' service were sifted to fill junior officer posts, while older men were retired as surplus members of their original units.

sentences.zh: 瓊進曰：「此非激勸之道，宿衛豈不勞乎？

translations.literal: Qiong advanced and said: "This is no way to encourage merit—is service in the palace guard not arduous?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiong objected: "That is no way to reward loyalty. Is palace duty not labor enough in itself?"

sentences.zh: 」自是八年者皆得敘補焉。

translations.literal: From then on, those with eight years of service were also allowed promotion and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter guardsmen with eight years of service were also eligible for promotion.

sentences.zh: 馬軍都校葛霸權步軍司，會以疾在告，令瓊兼領二司。

translations.literal: Ge Ba, company commander of the Horse Army, was acting head of the Foot Army Bureau; when he took sick leave, Qiong was ordered to hold both bureaus concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba of the horse guard was acting chief of the foot guard bureau; when illness kept him away, Qiong was ordered to command both services.

sentences.zh: 瓊從容上言曰：「臣衰老，儻又有犬馬之疾，則須一將總此二職。

translations.literal: Qiong calmly memorialized, saying: "I am old and failing; should I again suffer a dog-and-horse illness, one general will be needed to hold both these posts."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong submitted a measured memorial: "I am aging. Should illness strike me again, one general ought to be ready to hold both commands."

sentences.zh: 臣事先朝時，侍衛都虞候以上常至十員，職位相亞，易於遷改，且使軍伍熟其名望，邊藩緩急，亦可選用。

translations.literal: When I served the former court, there were often as many as ten officers from Chief Commandant of the Palace Guard upward; their ranks were nearly equal, transfers were easy, the army came to know their reputations, and in border emergencies they could be selected for use.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign there were often as many as ten officers from chief commandant of the palace guard upward. Their ranks were nearly equal, promotion was straightforward, the troops knew their names, and in a frontier crisis they could be drawn upon at once.

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以久疾求解兵柄，授檢校太尉、忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: Before long, because of long illness he asked to relinquish military command and was granted Honorary Grand Preceptor and Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, citing prolonged illness, he sought release from military command and was made honorary grand preceptor and military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，疾甚，上欲親臨問之，宰相不可，乃止。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year his illness grew severe; the emperor wished to visit him in person, but the chief ministers objected, and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his illness worsened. The emperor wished to call on him personally, but the chief ministers dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two; the post of Palace Attendant was conferred upon him posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 瓊不識字，曉達軍政，然頗自任，罕與副將參議。

translations.literal: Qiong could not read characters, yet understood military administration thoroughly; however he was rather self-willed and rarely consulted with his deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Though illiterate, Qiong had a thorough grasp of military affairs; yet he was headstrong and seldom took counsel from his deputies.

sentences.zh: 善訓諸子：繼勳、繼宣、繼忠、繼密、繼和、繼隆、繼元。

translations.literal: He trained his sons well: Jixun, Jixuan, Jizhong, Jimi, Jihe, Jilong, and Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his sons with discipline: Jixun, Jixuan, Jizhong, Jimi, Jihe, Jilong, and Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 繼勳、繼宣最知名。

translations.literal: Jixun and Jixuan were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, Jixun and Jixuan were the best known.

sentences.zh: 子 繼勳

translations.literal: Son: Jixun
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixun

sentences.zh: 繼勳，字紹先，初補右班殿直。

translations.literal: Jixun, styled Shaoxian, was at first appointed Right Company Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun, courtesy name Shaoxian, first entered service as a right-company palace guard.

sentences.zh: 儀狀頎偉，太宗見而異之，召問其家世，以瓊子對。

translations.literal: His bearing was tall and imposing; Taizong saw him and was struck by him, summoned and asked his family background, and learned he was Qiong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and striking in appearance, he caught Taizong's eye. Summoned and questioned about his lineage, he answered that he was Qiong's son.

sentences.zh: 擢寄班祗候，累遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Guard Company and rose through repeated transfers to Inner Hall Honored Company.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the imperial guard company and eventually rose to inner-hall honored company.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，王均據益州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, Wang Jun seized Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping, Wang Jun rebelled and held Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 以崇儀副使為益州兵馬都監、提舉西川諸州軍巡檢公事。

translations.literal: As Deputy Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial he was made Chief Military Supervisor of Yizhou and Commissioner for Inspection Affairs of the Armies of the Western Sichuan Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy commissioner of honored ceremonial he was made chief military supervisor of Yizhou and commissioner overseeing inspection of the armies of the western Sichuan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 招安使雷有終以兵五百授繼勳，守東郭二門，會賊攻彌牟砦，繼勳引兵轉鬥至嘉州，敗之，獲黃繖、金塗鎗以還。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Lei Youzhong gave Jixun five hundred troops to hold the eastern and outer city gates; when bandits attacked the Mimu Fort, Jixun led troops fighting in successive engagements to Jiazhou, defeated them, and returned with a yellow parasol and gilded spears as trophies.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Lei Youzhong assigned Jixun five hundred men to hold the eastern outer gates. When rebels assaulted Mimu Fort, Jixun fought through to Jiazhou, routed them, and returned bearing a yellow parasol and gilded spears as trophies.

sentences.zh: 有終益以勁兵復進攻二門，克之，乃建幟城上。

translations.literal: Youzhong added elite troops and again advanced to attack the two gates, captured them, and then raised banners atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong reinforced him with crack troops and again stormed the two gates. Once they fell, banners were raised on the walls.

sentences.zh: 諸將知城拔，有終乃引軍薄天長門，賊復來拒戰。

translations.literal: When the generals learned the city had been taken, Youzhong then led the army close to the Tianchang Gate; the bandits again came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the city had fallen, Youzhong pressed the army toward the Tianchang Gate, where the rebels sallied out to fight again.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，有終欲少休，繼勳曰：「賊窘矣，急擊之，無失也。

translations.literal: As dusk fell Youzhong wished to rest briefly; Jixun said: "The bandits are hard pressed—strike them at once; do not let the chance slip."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Youzhong wanted to pause, but Jixun urged: "The enemy is cornered. Press the attack now—do not let them escape."

sentences.zh: 」率十數騎鏖戰，身被數創，血濡甲；

translations.literal: Leading a dozen or so horsemen he fought fiercely; his body received several wounds and blood soaked his armor;
translations.idiomatic: At the head of a dozen horsemen he plunged into the melee, taking several wounds until blood soaked his armor;

sentences.zh: 馬死，更馬以進。

translations.literal: his horse died, and he changed horses and pressed on.
translations.idiomatic: when his horse was killed he mounted another and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 會入內都知秦翰來援，賊退保子城，不敢出。

translations.literal: Just then Inner Palace Director Qin Han came with reinforcements; the bandits withdrew to the inner citadel and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived under inner-palace director Qin Han. The rebels fell back into the inner citadel and dared not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 繼勳潛知賊欲夜遁，開圍使得潰去，均卒敗滅。

translations.literal: Jixun secretly learned the bandits intended to flee by night; he opened the encirclement and let them break out in disorder, and Wang Jun was ultimately defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning secretly that the rebels meant to flee by night, Jixun opened the ring and let them break out in confusion; Wang Jun was eventually crushed.

sentences.zh: 以功遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to commissioner of honored ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 賊餘黨保山藪中，時出剽劫，乃徙綿漢劍門路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Remnant bandits held the mountain thickets and from time to time came out to plunder and rob; he was then transferred to Chief Inspector of the Mian-Han-Jianmen Route.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants lurked in the hills and raided intermittently, so he was transferred to chief inspector of the Mian-Han-Jianmen route.

sentences.zh: 繼勳募惡少年偵賊動靜，窮躡岩穴，掩其不備，悉擒殺之。

translations.literal: Jixun recruited unruly youths to spy on the bandits' movements, pursued them relentlessly into cliff caves, and catching them unprepared captured and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun enlisted hard cases among local youths to track the rebels, chased them into their mountain lairs, and catching them off guard killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 又徙峽路鈐轄，還朝，遷洛苑使、幷代州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Controller of the Gorges Route, returned to court, and was promoted to Director of the Luoyang Park and Controller of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made controller of the gorges route, returned to court, and was promoted to director of the Luoyang park and controller of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 徙屯岢嵐軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison at Keilan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to garrison Keilan Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹聚兵五萬屯草城川，繼勳登高望之，謂軍使賈宗曰：「彼眾而陣不整，將不才也。

translations.literal: The Khitan massed fifty thousand troops at Caocheng River; Jixun climbed high and looked out, saying to Army Commissioner Jia Zong: "They are many but their formation is not orderly—their general lacks talent."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan concentrated fifty thousand men at Caocheng River, Jixun surveyed them from a height and told army commissioner Jia Zong: "They are numerous but their lines are ragged—their commander is no soldier."

sentences.zh: 我兵雖少，可以奇取勝。

translations.literal: Our troops though few can win by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Though we are fewer, we can win by a surprise stroke.

sentences.zh: 先伏兵山下，敵見我弱，必急攻我。

translations.literal: First hide troops below the hill; when the enemy sees us weak they will surely press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Hide men below the hill first. Seeing us weak, they will rush to attack.

sentences.zh: 我誘之南走，爾起乘之，當大潰。

translations.literal: I will lure them south in flight; you rise and strike them, and they should collapse in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I will feign retreat to the south. You rise and strike from ambush, and they should break completely.

sentences.zh: 」轉戰至寒光嶺，伏發，契丹果敗，相蹂躪死者萬餘人，獲馬、牛、橐駝甚眾。

translations.literal: Fighting in successive engagements they reached Hanguang Ridge; the ambush sprang and the Khitan were indeed defeated; trampling one another they died in numbers exceeding ten thousand; horses, cattle, and camels captured were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting through to Hanguang Ridge, the ambush was sprung and the Khitan routed. More than ten thousand perished in the stampede, and vast numbers of horses, cattle, and camels were taken.

sentences.zh: 遷弓箭庫使，賜金帶、錦袍，領榮州刺史，徙麟、府州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Bow and Arrow Store, granted a gold belt and brocade robe, held concurrently the prefecture of Rongzhou, and was transferred to Controller of Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the bow and arrow store, given a gold belt and brocade robe, made concurrent prefect of Rongzhou, and transferred to controller of Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 時屯兵河外，饋運不屬。

translations.literal: At that time troops were encamped beyond the Yellow River and supply transport was not connected.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then encamped west of the Yellow River with no steady supply line.

sentences.zh: 繼勳扼兔毛川，援送軍食，師乃濟。

translations.literal: Jixun held Tumaocuan, escorted and delivered army provisions, and only then could the army cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun seized control of Tumaocuan, convoyed grain to the army, and only then could the force cross.

sentences.zh: 徙知環州，又徙瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Huanzhou, then again to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Huanzhou, then Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，募富人出粟以給貧者。

translations.literal: At that time the year was famine-stricken; he recruited the wealthy to release grain to supply the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he persuaded wealthy households to release grain for the poor.

sentences.zh: 明年大稔，木生連理者四，郡人上治狀請留。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great harvest; four trees grew with conjoined trunks; the people of the commandery submitted a report on good governance asking that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The next year brought a bumper harvest and four trees with fused trunks—a sign of good rule for which the people petitioned to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 遷內藏庫使，以宮苑使奉使契丹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Inner Treasury and sent as Palace Park Commissioner on embassy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of the inner treasury, he was sent to the Khitan as palace park commissioner.

sentences.zh: 還，知定州，遷西上閤門使、昭州團練使，徙鄜延路鈐轄，坐市馬虧價失官。

translations.literal: On return he governed Dingzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Regimental Commissioner of Zhaozhou, was transferred to Controller of the Fuyan Route, and lost his office for undervaluing horses in purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he governed Dingzhou, rose to western upper gate commissioner and regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou, then controller of the Fuyan route, but lost his post for underpaying in horse purchases.

sentences.zh: 已而復為西上閤門使、榮州刺史、知冀州、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again made Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Prefect of Rongzhou, Governor of Jizhou, and concurrently Regimental Commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as western upper gate commissioner, prefect of Rongzhou, governor of Jizhou, and regimental commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 徙貝州，復知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Beizhou and again governed Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Beizhou before returning to govern Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭謝禮成，徙昭信軍節度使，為莊獻明肅太后山陵、莊懿太后園陵都總管，以老病乞骸骨。

translations.literal: When the Thanksgiving rites were completed he was transferred to Military Governor of the Zhaoxin Army, made Chief Superintendent of the mountain tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian Mingsu and the garden tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuangyi, and because of old age and illness asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After the thanksgiving rites he was made military governor of the Zhaoxin army and chief superintendent of the tombs of Empresses Zhuangxian Mingsu and Zhuangyi, then petitioned to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 召見便殿，許一子扶掖，俾勿拜，聽辭管軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience in the side hall; one son was permitted to support him; he was told not to bow; and he was allowed to resign from military command.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the side hall, he was permitted one son to steady him, excused from bowing, and allowed to relinquish command of the army.

sentences.zh: 授建雄軍節度使、知滑州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Governor of the Jianxiong Army and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Jianxiong army and governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 河水暴溢，齧堤岸，繼勳雖老，躬自督役，露坐河上，暮夜猶不輟，水乃殺怒，滑人德之。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks and gnawed at the dikes; though old, Jixun personally supervised the work, sitting in the open on the riverbank and continuing through night and dusk without pause; the waters then abated, and the people of Huazhou were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River flooded and ate at the dikes, Jixun though aged supervised the repairs in person, sitting exposed on the bank day and night until the waters subsided. The people of Huazhou honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，輟視朝一日，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight; court audiences were suspended for one day; Grand Preceptor was conferred upon him posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight. Court audiences were suspended for a day, and he was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 繼勳性謙，有機略，善撫禦士卒，臨戰輒勝。

translations.literal: Jixun was modest in nature, possessed stratagem, was skilled in comforting and controlling soldiers, and whenever he fought invariably won.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was modest, resourceful, and adept at winning soldiers' loyalty; in battle he was seldom defeated.

sentences.zh: 在蜀有威名，號「神將」。

translations.literal: In Shu he had a fearsome reputation and was called the "Divine General."
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan he enjoyed such renown that men called him the Divine General.

sentences.zh: 子 繼宣

translations.literal: Son: Jixuan
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixuan

sentences.zh: 繼宣，字舜舉。

translations.literal: Jixuan, styled Shunju.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan, courtesy name Shunju.

sentences.zh: 幼善騎射，頗工筆劄，知讀書。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled in horsemanship and archery, quite adept at writing, and knew how to read.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he excelled at riding and archery, wrote a fair hand, and had some learning.

sentences.zh: 以恩補西頭供奉官、惠民河巡督漕船。

translations.literal: By privilege he was appointed Western Attendant Palace Officer and Inspector of grain-transport ships on the Huimin Canal.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege of birth he was made western attendant palace officer and inspector of grain barges on the Huimin Canal.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑多盜，兼沿河巡檢捉賊，遷閤門祗候、邠州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: As famine that year bred many bandits, he was additionally made Riverine Inspector to capture thieves, was promoted to Gate Attendant and Chief Military Supervisor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year rife with banditry he was also made riverine inspector to hunt thieves, then promoted to gate attendant and chief military supervisor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 曹瑋守邠，數與言兵，薦其可用。

translations.literal: Cao Wei held Bin; he often discussed military matters with him and recommended him as usable.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cao Wei's command at Bin he often talked strategy with him, and Wei recommended him as capable.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，以內殿崇班為益州都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was made Inner Hall Honored Company and Chief Supervisor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianxing he was made inner-hall honored company and chief supervisor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀人富侈，元夕大張燈，知府薛奎戒以備盜，繼宣籍惡少年飲犒之，使夜中潛誌盜背，明日皆獲。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were rich and extravagant; on the Lantern Festival they hung many lamps; Prefect Xue Kui warned to guard against thieves; Jixuan registered unruly youths, treated them to drink and rewards, had them secretly mark thieves' backs at night, and the next day all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were lavish, lighting the city on the Lantern Festival. Prefect Xue Kui warned of thieves. Jixuan enlisted local rowdies, wined and rewarded them, had them secretly mark thieves' backs in the night, and by morning had them all.

sentences.zh: 歷磁、相、邢、洺都巡檢使，知安肅軍，徙保州。

translations.literal: He served successively as Chief Inspector of Ci, Xiang, Xing, and Ming, governed Ansu Army, and was transferred to Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief inspector of Ci, Xiang, Xing, and Ming, governed Ansu Army, and was transferred to Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮賓使、益州路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception and Military Controller of the Yizhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commissioner of ceremonial reception and military controller of the Yizhou route.

sentences.zh: 還，為西上閤門使、涇原路鈐轄兼安撫使、知渭州，遷四方館使、昭州刺史、知雄州。

translations.literal: On return he became Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Military Controller and Pacification Commissioner of the Jingyuan Route and Governor of Weizhou, and was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, Prefect of Zhaozhou, and Governor of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court he became western upper gate commissioner, military controller and pacification commissioner of the Jingyuan route and governor of Weizhou, then commissioner of the four directions hall, prefect of Zhaozhou, and governor of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元昊反，聲言侵關隴。

translations.literal: At first Yuan Hao rebelled, declaring he would invade Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao first rebelled, he announced an invasion of Guan and Long.

sentences.zh: 繼宣請備麟府。

translations.literal: Jixuan asked that Lin and Fu be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan petitioned to ready the defenses of Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，羌兵果入寇河外，陷豐州。

translations.literal: Before long Tangut troops indeed invaded beyond the Yellow River and captured Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tangut forces did cross the Yellow River and take Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢捧日天武四廂都指揮使、恩州團練使、知幷州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard, Regimental Commissioner of Enzhou, and Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the four wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard, regimental commissioner of Enzhou, and governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄寇麟府，繼宣帥兵營陵井，抵天門關。

translations.literal: Soon the enemy raided Lin and Fu; Jixuan led troops to encamp at Lingjing and reached Tianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy soon raided Lin and Fu, Jixuan marched to encamp at Lingjing and reached Tianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 是夕大雨，及河，師半濟，黑凌暴合，舟不得進，乃具牲酒為文以禱。

translations.literal: That evening heavy rain fell; reaching the river, the army was half across when black ice suddenly closed together and boats could not advance; he then prepared sacrificial animals and wine and wrote a prayer text.
translations.idiomatic: That night a downpour struck. At the river, with half the army across, black ice suddenly closed the channel and boats could not move. He offered sacrificial wine and composed a prayer.

sentences.zh: 已而凌解，師濟，進屯府谷，間遣勇士夜亂賊營。

translations.literal: Before long the ice broke; the army crossed; advancing he encamped at Fugu and from time to time sent brave men by night to throw the enemy camp into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The ice soon parted and the army crossed. He advanced to Fugu and sent raiders by night to sow chaos in the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 又募黥配廂軍，得二千餘人，號清邊軍，命偏將王凱主之。

translations.literal: He also recruited tattooed convicts assigned to the wing armies, obtaining more than two thousand men, called them the Clear-Border Army, and appointed the deputy general Wang Kai to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited more than two thousand tattooed convicts from the wing armies into a force called the Clear-Border Army under deputy commander Wang Kai.

sentences.zh: 軍次三松嶺，賊數萬眾圍之，清邊軍奮起，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: The army halted at Sansong Ridge; bandits numbering tens of thousands surrounded them; the Clear-Border Army rose fiercely and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Sansong Ridge tens of thousands of enemy troops surrounded them. The Clear-Border Army fought back and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 其相躪藉死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Those trampled and killed among them could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Uncounted more died in the crush.

sentences.zh: 築寧遠砦，相視地脈，鑿石出泉。

translations.literal: He built Ningyuan Fort, surveyed the lay of the land, and drilled through rock to bring forth a spring.
translations.idiomatic: He built Ningyuan Fort, read the terrain, and drilled rock until a spring appeared.

sentences.zh: 已而城五砦，遷眉州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he walled five forts, was transferred to Defender of Meizhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon walled five forts, was transferred to defender of Meizhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 范廷召

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從平李筠、李重進，轉本班都知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he followed in the pacification of Li Jun and Li Chongjin and was transferred to Chief of the Original Company.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years of Song he helped suppress Li Jun and Li Chongjin and rose to chief of his original company.

sentences.zh: 又從征太原，再轉散都頭、都虞候、領費州刺史。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Taiyuan and was twice transferred to Chief of the Loose Company, Chief Commandant, and concurrently Prefect of Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again at Taiyuan and was twice promoted—to chief of the loose company, chief commandant, and concurrent prefect of Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，以日騎軍都指揮使從平太原，征范陽。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, as Commander of the Sun-Cavalry Army he followed in the pacification of Taiyuan and the expedition against Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo, as commander of the sun-cavalry army he helped pacify Taiyuan and marched against Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 秦王廷美嘗遣親吏閻懷忠、趙瓊犒禁軍列校，廷召預焉，坐出為唐州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Tingmei once sent personal clerks Yan Huaizhong and Zhao Qiong to reward the palace guard company commanders; Tingzhao was among them and was punished by being sent out as Combined Horse-and-Foot Commander of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qin Tingmei sent personal clerks Yan Huaizhong and Zhao Qiong to reward palace guard officers, Tingzhao was implicated and was banished to combined horse-and-foot command at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，議北征，召入為馬步軍都軍頭、領平州刺史、幽州道前軍先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, when a northern expedition was debated, he was summoned in as Chief of Combined Horse and Foot Armies, concurrently Prefect of Pingzhou, and Vanguard Commander of the Youzhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, as a northern campaign was planned, he was recalled as chief of combined horse and foot armies, concurrent prefect of Pingzhou, and vanguard commander on the Youzhou route.

sentences.zh: 與賊遇固安南，破其眾三千，斬首千餘級，克固安、新城二縣，乘勝下涿州。

translations.literal: He met the enemy south of Gu'an, broke their force of three thousand, cut off more than a thousand heads, captured the two counties of Gu'an and Xincheng, and pressing the victory descended on Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: South of Gu'an he routed three thousand enemy troops, took more than a thousand heads, captured Gu'an and Xincheng, and pressed on to Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 廷召復與賊戰，中流矢，血漬甲縷，神色自若，督戰益急，詔褒之。

translations.literal: Tingzhao again fought the enemy, was struck by a flying arrow, blood soaked the threads of his armor, yet his expression remained calm and he pressed the battle all the more urgently; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao fought again, took an arrow through his armor, yet kept an unruffled face and drove the battle harder still. The throne issued praise.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷日騎右廂都指揮使、領本州圍練使，又遷左廂，移領高州。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to Commander of the Right Wing of the Sun-Cavalry Army and concurrently Regimental Commissioner of that prefecture, then transferred to the left wing and moved to hold concurrently Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he commanded the right wing of the sun-cavalry army and held the regimental commission of his prefecture, then shifted to the left wing and the regimental commission at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出為齊州防禦使，數月，授捧日天武四廂都指揮使、領澄州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he went out as Defender of Qizhou; after several months he was appointed Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard and concurrently Defender of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was posted as defender of Qizhou; within months he was made commander of the four wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard and defender of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉殿前都虞候、領涼州觀察使、鎮州副都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Chief Commandant of the Palace Front Guard, concurrently Surveillance Commissioner of Liangzhou and Deputy Deployment Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became chief commandant of the palace front guard, surveillance commissioner of Liangzhou, and deputy deployment commissioner at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 大破契丹三萬眾於徐河，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: He utterly defeated thirty thousand Khitan at Xu River and cut off several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu River he shattered thirty thousand Khitan and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，為平虜橋砦都部署，歷幷代、環慶兩路副部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was Deployment Commissioner of Pingluqiao Fort, and served successively as Deputy Deployment Commissioner of the Bing-Dai and Huanqing routes.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 he commanded Pingluqiao Fort and served as deputy deployment commissioner on the Bing-Dai and Huanqing routes.

sentences.zh: 至道中，遣將從五路討李繼遷，命廷召副李繼隆為環慶靈都部署。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era generals were dispatched on five routes to punish Li Jiqian; Tingzhao was ordered to serve under Li Jilong as Huanqing-Ling Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhidao, as five columns marched against Li Jiqian, Tingzhao was made deputy to Li Jilong as Huanqing-Ling deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廷召出延州路，與賊遇白池，獲米募軍主吃囉等兵器、鎧甲數萬。

translations.literal: Tingzhao went out by the Yanzhou route, met the enemy at Baichi, and captured weapons and armor numbering in the tens of thousands, including the Mi-recruited army chieftain Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao marched out on the Yanzhou route, met the enemy at Baichi, and captured tens of thousands of weapons and suits of armor, including the Mi-recruited chieftain Chiluo.

sentences.zh: 是役也，諸將失期，獨廷召與王超大小數十戰，屢克捷，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In that campaign the other generals missed their rendezvous; only Tingzhao and Wang Chao fought several dozen engagements large and small and repeatedly won; the emperor commended them.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign other generals missed their deadlines; only Tingzhao and Wang Chao fought dozens of actions and won repeatedly. The emperor commended them.

sentences.zh: 俄又為幷代兩路都部署。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again made Combined Deployment Commissioner of the Bing and Dai routes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made combined deployment commissioner of the Bing and Dai routes.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領河西軍節度，為定州行營都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Commander of the Palace Guard Horse Soldiers, concurrently Military Governor of the Hexi Army, and Field Headquarters Deployment Commissioner of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry, military governor of the Hexi army, and field headquarters deployment commissioner at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，契丹入塞，車駕北巡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping the Khitan entered the frontier passes; the imperial carriage toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 the Khitan crossed the border and the emperor marched north.

sentences.zh: 廷召與戰瀛州西，斬首二萬級，逐北至莫州東三十里，又斬首萬餘，奪其所掠老幼數萬口，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: Tingzhao fought west of Yingzhou, cut off twenty thousand heads, pursued north to thirty li east of Mozhou, cut off another ten thousand-plus heads, recovered several tens of thousands of old and young whom they had seized, and the Khitan fled away.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yingzhou Tingzhao took twenty thousand heads, pursued to thirty li east of Mozhou, took another ten thousand, recovered tens of thousands of captives, and drove the Khitan off.

sentences.zh: 師還，錄功加檢校太傅，益賦邑，又改殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was recorded and he was given the additional title of Honorary Grand Mentor, his fief was increased, and he was again changed to Commander of the Palace Front Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On return his service was rewarded with honorary grand mentor, an enlarged fief, and appointment as commander of the palace front guard.

sentences.zh: 四年正月被疾，車駕臨問，卒，年七十五，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited him in inquiry; he died at seventy-five; Palace Attendant was conferred upon him posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he fell ill. The emperor visited him at his bedside. He died at seventy-five and was posthumously made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 廷召在軍四十餘年，由顯德以來，凡親征，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Tingzhao was in the army more than forty years; from the Xiande era onward, whenever there was a personal expedition he never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao served more than forty years in the army. From the Xiande reign onward he never missed an imperial campaign.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，嘗出獵，有群鳥飛過，廷召發矢，並貫其三，觀者駭異。

translations.literal: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he once went hunting; a flock of birds flew past; Tingzhao loosed an arrow and pierced three at once; onlookers were startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: A fine horseman and archer, he once on a hunt shot a single arrow through three birds in flight, to the astonishment of all who watched.

sentences.zh: 性惡飛禽，所至處彈射殆絕。

translations.literal: By nature he hated flying birds; wherever he went he hunted them nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: He detested birds and hunted them nearly to extinction wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 尤不喜驢鳴，聞必擊殺之。

translations.literal: He especially disliked the braying of donkeys; whenever he heard it he invariably had the animal killed.
translations.idiomatic: He loathed the bray of donkeys and always ordered any braying beast killed.

sentences.zh: 子守均，至散員都虞候、演州刺史；

translations.literal: His son Shoujun rose to Chief Commandant of the Loose Company and Prefect of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoujun rose to chief commandant of the loose company and prefect of Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 守信，內殿承製、閤門祗候；

translations.literal: Shouxin, Inner Hall Artisan and Gate Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin became inner-hall artisan and gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 守宣，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Shouxuan, Inner Hall Honored Company;
translations.idiomatic: Shouxuan, inner-hall honored company;

sentences.zh: 守慶更名珪，後為西京作坊副使、淮南江浙荊湖制置發運副使。

translations.literal: Shouqing changed his name to Gui and later became Deputy Director of the Western Capital Workshops and Deputy Transport Commissioner for Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqing, who changed his name to Gui, later served as deputy director of the western capital workshops and deputy transport commissioner for Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 葛霸，真定人。

translations.literal: Ge Ba was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 姿表雄毅，善擊刺騎射。

translations.literal: His appearance was bold and stern; he was skilled in thrusting, riding, and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and imposing in bearing, he excelled at lance work, riding, and archery.

sentences.zh: 始事太宗於藩邸；

translations.literal: He first served Taizong at the princely residence;
translations.idiomatic: He entered Taizong's service while Taizong was still a prince;

sentences.zh: 踐阼，補殿前指揮使，稍遷本班都知，三遷至散員都虞候。

translations.literal: when Taizong ascended the throne he was appointed Palace Front Guard Commander, was gradually promoted to Chief of the Original Company, and through three promotions reached Chief Commandant of the Loose Company.
translations.idiomatic: on Taizong's accession he was made palace front guard commander, rose gradually to chief of the original company, and after three promotions reached chief commandant of the loose company.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，幽州之師失律，大補軍校，以霸為驍騎軍都指揮使、領檀州刺史，戍定州。

translations.literal: In Yongxi the army at Youzhou lost discipline; army officers were greatly replenished; Ba was made Commander of the Valiant Cavalry Army, concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou, and garrisoned at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Youzhou debacle in Yongxi, with ranks of officers refilled, Ba was made commander of the valiant cavalry army, concurrent prefect of Tanzhou, and posted to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇敵唐河，與戰，敗走之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He once met the enemy at Tang River, fought, routed and pursued them, and killed and captured in very great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At Tang River he met the enemy, routed them in pursuit, and killed or captured a great host.

sentences.zh: 俄召為御前忠佐馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Chief of the Imperial Front Loyal Assistant Combined Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as chief of the imperial front loyal-assistant combined horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出為博州團練使，歷潞、代二州部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he went out as Regimental Commissioner of Bozhou and served successively as Deployment Commissioner of Lu and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was posted as regimental commissioner of Bozhou and served as deployment commissioner at Lu and Dai.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，擢殿前都虞候、領潘州觀察使，為高陽關副都部署，進都部署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua he was promoted to Chief Commandant of the Palace Front Guard, concurrently Surveillance Commissioner of Panzhou, Deputy Deployment Commissioner of Gaoyang Pass, and then promoted to Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 1 he was promoted to chief commandant of the palace front guard and surveillance commissioner of Panzhou, made deputy then full deployment commissioner at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 凡七戰。

translations.literal: In all he fought seven battles.
translations.idiomatic: He fought seven battles in all.

sentences.zh: 召還，制授保順軍節度，典軍如故。

translations.literal: Recalled, by imperial order he was granted Military Governor of the Baoshun Army, commanding troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was by decree made military governor of the Baoshun army while retaining troop command.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮州都部署，徙天雄軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Deployment Commissioner of Zhenzhou and was transferred to the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as deployment commissioner at Zhenzhou, then transferred to the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，車駕勞師於大名，霸與石保吉同來覲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping the imperial carriage reviewed the troops at Daming; Ba came with Shi Baoji to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3 the emperor reviewed troops at Daming; Ba came with Shi Baoji to audience.

sentences.zh: 時康保裔沒於河間，即日以霸為貝、冀、高陽關前軍行營都部署。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Baoyi had perished at Hejian; that same day Ba was made Field Headquarters Deployment Commissioner of the Vanguard at Beizhou, Jizhou, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Baoyi fell at Hejian, Ba was that same day made vanguard field headquarters deployment commissioner for Beizhou, Jizhou, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 二月，就遷副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second month he was concurrently promoted to Deputy Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was also promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改邠寧、涇原、環慶三路都部署。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Combined Deployment Commissioner of the Binning, Jingyuan, and Huanqing routes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made combined deployment commissioner of the Binning, Jingyuan, and Huanqing routes.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使，領感德軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Commander of the Palace Guard Horse Soldiers and concurrently Military Governor of the Gande Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry and military governor of the Gande army.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，河決澶州橫壟埽，命為修河都部署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde the Yellow River broke through at Henglong Bank in Cizhou; he was ordered to be Chief Deployment Commissioner for River Repair.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 1 the Yellow River burst at Henglong Bank in Cizhou and he was ordered to direct river repairs.

sentences.zh: 未行，屬北邊有警，真宗議親征，以霸為駕前西面邢洺路都部署，又副李繼隆為駕前東面排陣使，駐澶州。

translations.literal: Before he set out the northern frontier had alarm; Zhenzong debated a personal expedition; Ba was made Western Route Deployment Commissioner before the Imperial Carriage on the Xing-Ming Route, and also served under Li Jilong as Eastern Route Battle Array Deputy before the Imperial Carriage, stationed at Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, alarms rose on the northern frontier. As Zhenzong contemplated marching in person, Ba was made western-route deployment commissioner before the imperial carriage on the Xing-Ming route and eastern-route battle-array deputy under Li Jilong, stationed at Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年召還，以功特加封邑。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled and his fief was specially increased for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled the next year, he received a special enlargement of his fief for his service.

sentences.zh: 上言朝廷居明德心喪，尚遏音樂，請停迎授之制，奏可。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the court was in the heart-mourning period for Empress Mingde and still restrained music; he asked to stop the ceremony of welcoming and investing officials; the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that with the court still in mourning for Empress Mingde and music curtailed, the ceremony of welcoming and investing officials should be suspended. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以霸久典兵，年且老，罷軍職，授昭德軍節度、幷代都部署。

translations.literal: That winter, because Ba had long held military command and was also old, his military post was removed; he was granted Military Governor of the Zhaode Army and Combined Bing-Dai Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, because Ba had held command too long and was aging, he was relieved of military office and made military governor of the Zhaode army and combined Bing-Dai deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣有隸麾下者，頗擾軍民，霸昏耄，為所罔，真宗知之，故有是召。

translations.literal: At that time there were court officials subordinate to his command who greatly harassed soldiers and civilians; Ba was senile and deceived by them; Zhenzong knew this, and therefore issued this summons.
translations.idiomatic: Some court officials under his command were harassing soldiers and civilians; senile and misled, Ba was recalled for that reason.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，徙知耀州。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he was transferred to govern Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That summer in the fourth year he was made governor of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 霸雖懦，然能謹直自持。

translations.literal: Though Ba was timid, he could nevertheless maintain himself with scrupulous integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Timid though he was, Ba still held himself to a strict standard of integrity.

sentences.zh: 會東封，表求扈蹕。

translations.literal: When the eastern tour of Mount Tai occurred he memorialized asking to accompany the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern tour of Mount Tai he petitioned to join the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 既以疾不能從，車駕還次衛南，疾少間，迎謁行在。

translations.literal: Because illness prevented him from following, when the imperial carriage returned and halted at Weinan his illness eased somewhat and he came to greet the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from the tour, but when the emperor halted at Weinan on the return, he recovered enough to come and greet the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其意，勞問久之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his intent and questioned and consoled him at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and questioned and consoled him at length.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十五，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before long he died at seventy-five; Grand Preceptor was conferred upon him posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at seventy-five and was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子懷信、懷正、懷敏、懷煦。

translations.literal: His sons were Huaixin, Huaizheng, Huaimin, and Huaixu.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Huaixin, Huaizheng, Huaimin, and Huaixu.

sentences.zh: 懷信至如京副使；

translations.literal: Huaixin rose to Deputy Commissioner of the Capital Grain Office;
translations.idiomatic: Huaixin rose to deputy commissioner of the capital grain office;

sentences.zh: 懷煦，內殿承制；

translations.literal: Huaixu, Inner Hall Artisan;
translations.idiomatic: Huaixu, inner-hall artisan;

sentences.zh: 懷正，博州團練使、知滄、莫二州。

translations.literal: Huaizheng, Regimental Commissioner of Bozhou and Governor of Cang and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizheng, regimental commissioner of Bozhou and governor of Cang and Mo.

translations.literal: 〈Son〉
translations.idiomatic: Son

sentences.zh: 懷敏

translations.literal: Huaimin
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin.

sentences.zh: 懷敏以蔭授西頭供奉官，加閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Huaimin by privilege of birth was appointed Western Attendant Palace Officer and added as Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin entered service by privilege as western attendant palace officer and gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 歷同提點益州路刑獄、襄鄧都巡檢。

translations.literal: He served successively as Co-Commissioner for Criminal Affairs of the Yizhou Route and Chief Inspector of Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as co-commissioner for criminal affairs on the Yizhou route and chief inspector of Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，知隰、莫、保三州，累遷東染院使、康州刺史、知雄州，就遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: Sent on embassy to the Khitan, he governed Xi, Mo, and Bao; through repeated promotions he became Director of the Eastern Dyeing Bureau, Prefect of Kangzhou, Governor of Xiongzhou, and was concurrently promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to the Khitan he governed Xi, Mo, and Bao, rose to director of the eastern dyeing bureau, prefect of Kangzhou, and governor of Xiongzhou, and was promoted to western upper gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上《平燕策》。

translations.literal: He submitted a "Plan for Pacifying Yan."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a Plan for Pacifying Yan.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，塘水涸，懷敏慮契丹使至測知其廣深，乃擁界河水注之，塘復如故。

translations.literal: As famine struck that year the moat water dried up; Huaimin feared Khitan envoys would come and measure its breadth and depth; he therefore diverted border-river water to fill it, and the moat was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year the moat ran dry. Fearing Khitan envoys would measure its depth, Huaimin diverted border-river water to refill it.

sentences.zh: 召對邊事，復還雄州，改萊州團練使。

translations.literal: Summoned to discuss frontier affairs, he returned again to Xiongzhou and was changed to Regimental Commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Called to discuss frontier affairs, he returned to Xiongzhou and was made regimental commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 濁流砦兵叛，殺官吏潰去，懷敏發兵掩襲，盡誅其黨。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Zhuoliu Fort rebelled, killed officials, and fled in disorder; Huaimin sent troops in a surprise attack and executed the whole faction.
translations.idiomatic: When troops at Zhuoliu Fort mutinied, killed officials, and fled, Huaimin sent a raiding force and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 在雄州五年，徙滄州。

translations.literal: After five years at Xiongzhou he was transferred to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After five years governing Xiongzhou he was posted to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為王德用妹婿，德用貶，亦絳知滁州。

translations.literal: Huaimin was the brother-in-law of Wang Deyong; when Deyong was demoted, Huaimin was also reduced and made Governor of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was Wang Deyong's brother-in-law; when Deyong was demoted, Huaimin was reduced to governor of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵，起為涇原路馬步軍副總管兼涇原秦鳳兩路經略、安撫副使。

translations.literal: When war was waged in Shaanxi he was raised to Deputy Chief of Combined Horse and Foot of the Jingyuan Route and concurrently Deputy Commissioner for Strategy and Pacification of the Jingyuan and Qin-Feng routes.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Shaanxi he was recalled as deputy chief of Jingyuan horse and foot and deputy commissioner for strategy and pacification of Jingyuan and Qin-Feng.

sentences.zh: 既入對，以曹瑋嘗所被介胄賜之，令制置鄜延、環慶兩路存廢砦柵。

translations.literal: After entering audience he was given the armor once worn by Cao Wei and ordered to decide which forts and stockades on the Fuyan and Huanqing routes should be kept or abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: On audience he was given armor once worn by Cao Wei and ordered to decide which forts on the Fuyan and Huanqing routes to keep or abandon.

sentences.zh: 擢龍神衛四廂都指揮、眉州防禦使、本路副都總管、知涇原。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, Defender of Meizhou, Deputy Chief Commander of that route, and Governor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the four wings of the dragon spirit guard, defender of Meizhou, deputy chief commander of the route, and governor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷捧日天武四廂都指揮使、鄜延路副都總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard and Deputy Chief Commander of the Fuyan Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander of the four wings of the Sun-Held Heavenly Martial Guard and deputy chief commander of the Fuyan route.

sentences.zh: 進殿前都虞候、知延州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Chief Commandant of the Palace Front Guard and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to chief commandant of the palace front guard and governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹言其猾懦不知兵，復徙涇原路兼招討、經略、安撫副使。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan said he was cunning, timid, and ignorant of military affairs; he was again transferred to the Jingyuan Route as concurrently Deputy Commissioner for Punitive Campaigns, Strategy, and Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan called him cunning, timid, and unfit for command; he was shifted back to the Jingyuan route as deputy commissioner for punitive campaigns, strategy, and pacification.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，元昊寇鎮戎軍，懷敏出瓦亭砦，督砦主都監許思純、環慶路都監劉賀、天聖砦主張貴，及緣邊都巡檢使向進、劉湛、趙瑜等禦敵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Yuan Hao raided Zhenrong Army; Huaimin went out from Wating Fort and directed Fort Commander and Supervisor Xu Sichun, Huanqing Route Supervisor Liu He, Tiansheng Fort Commander Zhang Gui, and the frontier chief inspectors Xiang Jin, Liu Zhan, and Zhao Yu to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 2, when Yuan Hao attacked Zhenrong Army, Huaimin marched from Wating Fort and directed fort commander Xu Sichun, Huanqing supervisor Liu He, Tiansheng fort commander Zhang Gui, and frontier inspectors Xiang Jin, Liu Zhan, and Zhao Yu against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 軍次安邊砦，給芻秣未絕，懷敏輒離軍，夜至開遠堡北一里而舍。

translations.literal: The army halted at Anbian Fort; fodder had not yet ceased being issued when Huaimin abruptly left the army and by night reached a camp one li north of Kaiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Anbian Fort before fodder issue was even complete, Huaimin abruptly left the army and camped a li north of Kaiyuan Fort that night.

sentences.zh: 既而自鎮戎軍西南，又先引從騎百餘以前，承受趙正曰：「敵近，不可輕進。

translations.literal: Then from the southwest of Zhenrong Army he again led more than a hundred attendant horsemen ahead; the staff officer Zhao Zheng said: "The enemy is near—one must not advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Then from southwest of Zhenrong Army he again rode ahead with a hundred-odd followers. Staff officer Zhao Zheng warned: "The enemy is close—we must not advance rashly."

sentences.zh: 」懷敏乃少止。

translations.literal: Huaimin then halted briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin paused briefly.

sentences.zh: 日暮趨養馬城，與知鎮戎軍曹英及涇原路都監李知和王保王文、鎮戎軍都監李嶽、西路都巡檢使趙璘等會兵。

translations.literal: At dusk he hurried to Yangma City and joined forces with Zhenrong Army Governor Cao Ying, Jingyuan Route Supervisor Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Zhenrong Army Supervisor Li Yue, and Western Route Chief Inspector Zhao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he rushed to Yangma City and joined Cao Ying, governor of Zhenrong Army, Jingyuan supervisor Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Zhenrong supervisor Li Yue, and western-route chief inspector Zhao Lin.

sentences.zh: 聞元昊徙軍新壕外，懷敏議質明襲之，乃命諸命將分四路趣定川砦：劉湛、向進出西水口，涇原路都監趙珣出蓮華堡，曹英、李知和出劉璠堡，懷敏出定西堡。

translations.literal: Hearing Yuan Hao had moved his army outside the new moat, Huaimin planned a dawn raid and ordered the commanders to advance by four routes toward Dingchuan Fort: Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin by the West Water Mouth, Jingyuan Supervisor Zhao Xun by Lianhua Fort, Cao Ying and Li Zhihe by Liu Fan Fort, and Huaimin by Dingxi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Yuan Hao had shifted outside the new moat, Huaimin planned a dawn strike and divided his commanders toward Dingchuan Fort: Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin by West Water Mouth, Zhao Xun by Lianhua Fort, Cao Ying and Li Zhihe by Liu Fan Fort, and Huaimin by Dingxi Fort.

sentences.zh: 知和與英督軍夜發。

translations.literal: Zhihe and Ying supervised the army setting out by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhihe and Cao Ying led their columns out by night.

sentences.zh: 翌日，湛、進行次趙福堡，遇敵，戰不勝，保向家峽，懷敏使珣、英並鎮戎軍西路巡檢李良臣、孟淵援之。

translations.literal: The next day Zhan and Jin halted at Zhaofu Fort, met the enemy, fought without victory, and held Xiangjia Gorge; Huaimin sent Xun and Ying together with Zhenrong Army Western Route Inspectors Li Liangchen and Meng Yuan to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin halted at Zhaofu Fort, met the enemy, failed to win, and fell back to Xiangjia Gorge. Huaimin sent Zhao Xun and Cao Ying with western-route inspectors Li Liangchen and Meng Yuan to their aid.

sentences.zh: 俄報敵已拔柵逾邊壕，懷敏入保定川砦，敵毀板橋，斷其歸路，別為二十四道以過軍，環圍之。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the enemy had pulled up palisades and crossed the border moat; Huaimin entered Baodingchuan Fort; the enemy destroyed the pontoon bridge and cut off the return route, made twenty-four separate paths for troops to cross, and encircled them on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Word soon came that the enemy had torn up palisades and crossed the border ditch. Huaimin entered Baodingchuan Fort. The enemy destroyed the pontoon bridge, cut off retreat, opened twenty-four crossing paths, and surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 又絕定川水泉上流，以饑渴其眾。

translations.literal: They also cut off the upper reaches of the Dingchuan springs to starve and thirst the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: They also dammed the upper reaches of the Dingchuan springs to thirst the army.

sentences.zh: 劉賀率蕃兵門於河西，不勝，餘眾潰去。

translations.literal: Liu He led Tangut troops to hold the gate west of the river, was defeated, and the remainder fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He led Tangut auxiliaries to hold the west-bank gate, was beaten, and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為中軍屯塞門東偏，英等陣東北隅。

translations.literal: Huaimin as central army encamped on the eastern flank of Saimen; Ying and the others formed battle lines in the northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin encamped the center on the east side of Saimen; Cao Ying and the others formed on the northeast.

sentences.zh: 敵自褊江三、葉燮會出，四面環之。

translations.literal: The enemy came out from the junction of Bianjiang and Yexie and surrounded them on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sallied from Bianjiang and Yexie and closed in on four sides.

sentences.zh: 先以銳兵衝中軍，不動，回擊英軍。

translations.literal: First with sharp troops they charged the central army without moving it, then turned to strike Ying's army.
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops first struck the center without breaking it, then wheeled to hit Cao Ying's wing.

sentences.zh: 會黑風起東北，部伍相失，陣遂擾。

translations.literal: Just then a black wind rose from the northeast; units lost one another and the formation was thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: A black gale rose from the northeast; units lost contact and the formation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 士卒攀城堞爭入，英面被流矢，仆壕中，懷敏部兵見之亦奔駭。

translations.literal: Soldiers climbed the battlements struggling to enter; Ying's face was struck by a flying arrow and he fell into the moat; Huaimin's troops seeing this also fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers scrambled over the ramparts to get inside. Cao Ying took an arrow in the face and fell into the ditch. Huaimin's men panicked at the sight and fled.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為眾蹂躪幾死，輿致甕城，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: Huaimin was nearly trampled to death by the crowd, was carried into Weng City, and after a long time revived.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was nearly trampled to death, was carried into Weng City, and long afterward came to.

sentences.zh: 復選士據門橋，揮手刃以拒入城者。

translations.literal: He again selected soldiers to hold the gate bridge, waving blades to repel those trying to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted picked men on the gate bridge, slashing at anyone trying to force entry.

sentences.zh: 趙珣等以騎軍四合禦敵，敵眾稍卻，然大軍無鬥志。

translations.literal: Zhao Xun and others with cavalry on four sides resisted the enemy; the enemy force slightly withdrew, yet the main army had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xun and others rallied cavalry on four sides and the enemy drew back slightly, but the main army had lost its will to fight.

sentences.zh: 珣馳入，勸懷敏還軍中。

translations.literal: Xun galloped in and urged Huaimin to return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xun rode in and urged Huaimin back to the army.

sentences.zh: 是夕，敵聚火圍城四隅，臨西北呼曰：「爾得非總管廳點陣圖者邪？

translations.literal: That evening the enemy gathered fires around the four corners of the city; facing the northwest they shouted: "Are you not the one who drew up battle arrays in the commander's hall?"
translations.idiomatic: That night the enemy lit fires on all four sides of the walls and shouted from the northwest: "Are you not the man who plotted battle arrays in the commander's hall?"

sentences.zh: 爾固能軍，乃入我圍中，今復何往！

translations.literal: You indeed know how to command armies—yet you entered our encirclement; where can you go now!
translations.idiomatic: You fancy yourself a commander—yet you walked into our trap. Where will you run now!

sentences.zh: 」夜四鼓，懷敏召曹英、趙珣、李知和、王保、王文、許思純、劉賀、李良臣、趙瑜計議，莫知所出，遂謀結陣走鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night Huaimin summoned Cao Ying, Zhao Xun, Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Xu Sichun, Liu He, Li Liangchen, and Zhao Yu to deliberate; none knew what to do; they then planned to form ranks and flee to Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch Huaimin summoned Cao Ying, Zhao Xun, Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Xu Sichun, Liu He, Li Liangchen, and Zhao Yu. With no plan in sight, they resolved to break out toward Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴，懷敏自諭：「親軍左右及在後者皆毋得動，平明，從吾往安西堡。

translations.literal: At cockcrow Huaimin announced himself: "Personal guard left and right and those in the rear must not move; at dawn follow me to Anxi Fort."
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow Huaimin announced: "Personal guards and the rear must not stir. At dawn follow me to Anxi Fort."

sentences.zh: 以英、珣為先鋒，賀、思純為左右翼，知和為殿，聽中軍鼓乃得行。

translations.literal: With Ying and Xun as vanguard, He and Sichun as left and right wings, and Zhihe as rearguard, they were to march only on hearing the central army drum.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ying and Zhao Xun would lead, Liu He and Xu Sichun would cover the flanks, Li Zhihe the rear, and none were to move until the center drum sounded.

sentences.zh: 」至卯，鼓未作，懷敏先上馬，而大軍按堵未動。

translations.literal: By the mao hour the drum had not sounded; Huaimin mounted first, yet the main army remained still in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the drum had not sounded, yet Huaimin mounted first while the main army still stood in place.

sentences.zh: 懷敏周麾者再，將徑去，有執鞚者勸不可，懷敏不得已而還。

translations.literal: Huaimin circled and waved twice, was about to ride straight away; one who held his reins urged that he must not; Huaimin had no choice but to return.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin rode the line twice waving his command, about to bolt; a man holding his reins begged him to stay, and he unwillingly turned back.

sentences.zh: 使參謀郭京等取芻城中，未至，懷敏復上馬，叱執轡者使去，不聽，拔劍且擊之，士遂散。
