translations.literal: He sent staff officer Guo Jing and others to fetch fodder in the city; before they arrived Huaimin mounted again, shouted at those holding the reins to let go, and when they would not listen drew his sword and struck at them; the soldiers then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent staff officer Guo Jing to fetch fodder inside the walls. Before they returned Huaimin mounted again, ordered the reins let go, and when they refused slashed at them with his sword. The troops broke ranks.

sentences.zh: 懷敏驅馬東南馳二百里，至長城壕，路已斷，敵周圍之，遂與諸將皆遇害。

translations.literal: Huaimin drove his horse southeast for two hundred li to the Great Wall moat; the road was already cut off; the enemy surrounded them; he and the generals all met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin galloped southeast two hundred li to the Great Wall ditch. The road was cut; the enemy closed in; he and his generals were killed.

sentences.zh: 餘軍九千四百餘人，馬六百餘匹，為敵所斷。

translations.literal: The remaining army of more than nine thousand four hundred men and more than six hundred horses was cut off by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: More than nine thousand four hundred troops and six hundred horses were lost to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 其子宗晟與趙正、郭京、承受王昭明等還保定川。

translations.literal: His son Zongsheng together with Zhao Zheng, Guo Jing, staff officer Wang Zhaoming, and others returned to Baodingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongsheng, with Zhao Zheng, Guo Jing, staff officer Wang Zhaoming, and others, made it back to Baodingchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，懷敏令軍中步兵毋得動，及前陣已去，後軍多不知者，故皆得存。

translations.literal: At first Huaimin had ordered the infantry in the army not to move; when the vanguard had already gone, the rear army for the most part did not know and therefore all survived.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin had ordered the infantry not to move. When the vanguard fled, the rear ranks mostly did not know and so survived.

sentences.zh: 時韓質、郝從政、胡息以兵六千保蓮華堡，劉湛、向進兵一千保向家峽，皆不赴援。

translations.literal: At that time Han Zhi, Hao Congzheng, and Hu Xi with six thousand troops held Lianhua Fort; Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin with one thousand troops held Xiangjia Gorge; none came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhi, Hao Congzheng, and Hu Xi held Lianhua Fort with six thousand men; Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin held Xiangjia Gorge with one thousand. Neither column came to help.

sentences.zh: 於是敵長驅抵渭州，幅員六七百里，焚蕩廬舍，屠掠民畜而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the enemy drove straight to Weizhou across six or seven hundred li, burning and destroying houses and slaughtering and seizing people and livestock as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then swept six or seven hundred li to Weizhou, burning settlements and slaughtering people and livestock as they went.

sentences.zh: 奏至，帝嗟悼久之，贈懷敏鎮戎軍節度使兼太尉，英、知和、珣、保、文、質、嶽、貴、璘、思純、良臣及同時戰沒者，及涇原巡檢楊遵、籠竿城巡檢姚奭、涇原都巡檢司監押董謙、同巡檢唐斌、指使霍達，皆贈官有差。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor mourned long; Huaimin was posthumously granted Military Governor of Zhenrong Army and concurrently Grand Preceptor; Ying, Zhihe, Xun, Bao, Wen, Zhi, Yue, Gui, Lin, Sichun, Liangchen, and those who fell in battle at the same time, together with Jingyuan Inspector Yang Zun, Longgan Fort Inspector Yao Shang, Jingyuan Chief Inspector Superintendent Dong Qian, Co-Inspector Tang Bin, and Commanding Officer Huo Da, all received posthumous offices in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court the emperor grieved long. Huaimin was posthumously made military governor of Zhenrong Army and grand preceptor. Cao Ying, Li Zhihe, Zhao Xun, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Han Zhi, Li Yue, Zhang Gui, Zhao Lin, Xu Sichun, Li Liangchen, and others killed in the battle, with Jingyuan inspector Yang Zun, Longgan fort inspector Yao Shang, inspector superintendent Dong Qian, co-inspector Tang Bin, and commanding officer Huo Da, all received posthumous honors in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 復降向進等官，落郝從政、趙瑜職。

translations.literal: Xiang Jin and others were again demoted in rank; Hao Congzheng and Zhao Yu were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Jin and others were demoted; Hao Congzheng and Zhao Yu were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 懷敏通時事，善候人情，故多以才薦之。

translations.literal: Huaimin understood current affairs and was skilled at reading people's feelings; therefore many recommended him for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was politically astute and good at reading men, which is why so many praised his talents.

sentences.zh: 及用為將，而輕率昧於應變，遂至覆軍。

translations.literal: Yet when employed as a general he was rash and blind to changing circumstances, and thus brought about the destruction of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a field commander he was reckless and slow to adapt, and so destroyed his army.

sentences.zh: 帝念之，賜諡忠隱。

translations.literal: The emperor remembered him and granted the posthumous name Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still held him in regard and granted the posthumous name Loyal and Reserved.

sentences.zh: 子宗晟、宗壽、宗禮、宗師，皆遷官。

translations.literal: His sons Zongsheng, Zongshou, Zongli, and Zongshi were all promoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zongsheng, Zongshou, Zongli, and Zongshi were all promoted.

sentences.zh: 論曰：真宗澶淵之役，高瓊之功亦盛矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In Emperor Zhenzong's Chanyuan campaign, Gao Qiong's merit was also great.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In Zhenzong's Chanyuan campaign, Gao Qiong's service was likewise great.

sentences.zh: 范廷召年十八，能手刃父仇；

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao at eighteen could with his own hand slay his father's enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao at eighteen avenged his father with his own hand;

sentences.zh: 瓊將磔於市，幸以逃免；

translations.literal: Qiong was about to be dismembered in the marketplace and fortunately escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiong escaped dismemberment in the marketplace by a hair's breadth;

sentences.zh: 葛霸善擊刺馬射，給事藩邸，皆非素習韜略者也，及其出身戎行，迭居節鎮，而卓有可觀，由所遇之得其時也。

translations.literal: Ge Ba was skilled in thrusting and horse archery and served at the princely residence—none of them had originally studied strategy; yet when they entered military service and in succession held provincial commands, their achievements were notably worthy, because the times they met were favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba excelled at arms and served in the princely household—none had trained in strategy. Yet once they took to the field and rose to provincial command, each achieved much, for fortune favored their hour.

sentences.zh: 或謂瓊頗自用，謀議不及參佐，而洞曉軍政；

translations.literal: Some say Qiong was rather self-willed, that in planning he did not reach his staff officers, yet he thoroughly understood military administration;
translations.idiomatic: Some say Qiong was willful and seldom consulted his staff, yet understood war administration thoroughly;

sentences.zh: 霸雖失於巽懦，而能謹直自持；

translations.literal: Ba though failing in timidity and compliance could nevertheless maintain scrupulous integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Ba, though timid and yielding, still kept himself honest;

sentences.zh: 廷召性雖癖，在軍中四十年，累從征討，所至有功：皆不害其為驍果也。

translations.literal: Tingzhao though eccentric in nature, in forty years in the army repeatedly followed campaigns and wherever he went had merit: none of this prevented his being bold and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao, for all his eccentricities, served forty years in the field with merit wherever he fought—eccentricity did not diminish his valor.

sentences.zh: 廷召諸子，珪為最賢，霸子懷敏以戰死，固皆足稱。

translations.literal: Among Tingzhao's sons Gui was the most worthy; Ba's son Huaimin died in battle—they are all truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Of Tingzhao's sons Gui was the finest; Ba's son Huaimin died in battle—each in his way deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 若繼宣、繼勳之將業，則過其父遠甚，此「克勤敏功鍾慶之碑」所由以立歟！

translations.literal: As for Jixuan and Jixun's achievements as generals, they far surpassed their father—was this not why the stele "Accumulated Diligence, Merit, and Gathered Blessings" was erected!
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan and Jixun as generals far outshone their father—is that not why the stele "He Who Toils Diligently and Wins Merit Gathers Blessings" was raised!

sentences.zh: 夫以三子之自樹如此，而不得與狄青、郭逵同日而論者，豈非拳勇之有餘，而器識之不足也歟！

translations.literal: That these three sons should have established themselves so, yet not be spoken of in the same breath as Di Qing and Guo Kui—was it not because their raw courage was more than enough while their breadth of judgment fell short!
translations.idiomatic: Men who built careers such as these yet cannot stand beside Di Qing and Guo Kui—does this not show courage in abundance but judgment too small?
